elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.
elements.evidence: The added sentence permits Corio to terminate the Agreement for convenience and is not limited to a term-end date.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience requires no more than thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Commerce One may unilaterally elect to extend the notice period from 30 days to 60 days, so Corio does not have an unconditional 30-day termination right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly requires “prior written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Commerce One must “refund any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of termination,” which provides the required pro-rata economic result.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Commerce One receives no mid-term convenience-termination right. Its existing without-cause right is limited to preventing renewal at the expiration of the applicable term; the breach and insolvency rights are for cause.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Corio may terminate for convenience without waiting until the end of the five-year initial term or a renewal term.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience is subject to no more than sixty (60) to ninety (90) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The maximum operative notice period is 60 days if Commerce One exercises its election; otherwise the more customer-favorable 30-day period applies. The clause never requires more than 60 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied with a fee of zero.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise a convenience-based termination or nonrenewal right only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Commerce One may prevent renewal only upon expiration of the initial or applicable renewal term and has no mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' prior notice to exercise its term-end convenience-based termination or nonrenewal right.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits either party, including Commerce One, to prevent renewal on only 30 days' prior written notice.

result.reason: The redline adds a customer convenience right and the required prepaid-fee refund, while preserving the unrelated for-cause termination provisions. It fails the preferred position because Vendor can extend Customer's notice period to 60 days. It also fails the complete fallback because Vendor retains a term-end nonrenewal right on 30 rather than 90 days' notice. The parenthetical Vendor-election mechanism is also less clear than stating a single applicable notice period and how or when any election must be exercised.
